ledger_metadata.title: Primary Reading and Authenticity Audit Ledger for Four Foundational Nuclear Isomer Reviews
ledger_metadata.audit_framework: AGENTS.md Scientific Evidence & Bounded Verification Rules
principles: PyMuPDF chunk-wise sequential reading in blocks of 6-8 physical pages
No blanket claim of 100% full verification of all figures, sub-panels, references, or raw data
Explicit recording of actual topics, locators, checked figures/equations, and unverified scope per chunk
Distinguish author review compilations from direct original measurements
Identify and remove overstrong/unsubstantiated claims (e.g., universal f_nu=100, Sn all-isotope U-shape, unlocated superheavy 'several MeV', and 'zero-effect ended all experiments')
Disclose author dependencies and potential conflicts of interest (especially Carroll & Chiara 2024 regarding 93mMo NEEC)

documents.title: Energy traps in atomic nuclei
documents.canonical_source: P. Walker and G. Dracoulis, Nature 399, 35-40 (1999)

actual_topics: Introduction and high-spin isomer discovery context (p. 35)
Classification of energy traps: shape isomers, spin traps, K traps (pp. 35-36, Fig. 1)
Box 1: Isomer half-lives, widths, and Weisskopf single-particle benchmarks (p. 37)
Nuclide distribution of isomers with T1/2 > 1 s (p. 36, Fig. 2)
Reaction mechanisms: fusion-evaporation, partial fusion / fragmentation, deep-inelastic (p. 37, Fig. 3)
Multi-quasiparticle states, pairing blocking, and rigid-body moment of inertia limit in 178Hf (pp. 37-38, Fig. 4)
K-forbiddenness definition nu = Delta K - lambda and Löbner empirical rule of thumb f_nu ~ 100 (p. 38)
Systematic breakdown of Löbner rule: 179W Delta K=14, f_nu=2 anomaly (rate 10^20 faster) and triaxial gamma-tunneling mechanism (pp. 38-39, Fig. 5)
Statistical level density at high excitation energy and chance near-degeneracy (p. 39, Fig. 6)
Applications: induced de-excitation, X-ray pumping, Collins et al. 1999 178m2Hf report, and gamma-ray laser prospects (pp. 39-40)
References 1-56 (p. 40)
which_figures_or_equations_checked: Figure 1: Potential energy as a function of nuclear variables for shape isomer, spin trap, and K trap (p. 35)
Figure 2: Chart of atomic nuclei showing long-lived (T1/2 > 1 s) isomers (p. 36)
Figure 3: Reaction mechanisms for isomer production (p. 37)
Figure 4: Velocity fields and rotational band built on 16+ 31-yr isomer in 178Hf (p. 38)
Figure 5: Reduced hindrance f_nu vs isomer excitation energy relative to rotor (p. 38)
Figure 6: Multi-quasiparticle states and statistical level density in 178Hf (p. 38/39)
Box 1: Formulas Gamma*T1/2 = hbar*ln2 ~ 4.6e-16 eV*s and T(E_lambda) proportional to E_gamma^(2*lambda+1) (p. 37)
K-hindrance formula: nu = Delta K - lambda; f_nu = (F_W)^(1/nu) ~ 100 (rule of thumb) (p. 38)
unverified_scope: Individual data points and pixel-level curve positions in Fig. 2 (nuclear chart) and Fig. 5 (scatter plot of Hf/W/Os reduced hindrances)
Underlying experimental raw coincidence spectra and detector calibrations from ANU 14UD and Gammasphere
Full re-examination of all 56 cited primary literature papers back to their original experiment logs
Supplementary experimental details not published in the 6-page Nature print article
audited_corrections: Verified exact printed page numbers as Nature 399, 35-40 (6 physical pages)
Toned down the claim of universal f_nu ~ 100: the text explicitly treats f_nu ~ 100 as an empirical 'rule of thumb' (Löbner 1968) and focuses on its dramatic breakdown (e.g. f_nu = 2 in 179W)

Distinguished what Walker & Dracoulis wrote in 1999 regarding Collins et al. (cited as an 'encouraging advance' with theoretical caveats) from subsequent multi-laboratory disproofs that unfolded in 2001-2004

documents.title: Review of metastable states in heavy nuclei
documents.canonical_source: G. D. Dracoulis, P. M. Walker, and F. G. Kondev, Rep. Prog. Phys. 79, 076301 (2016)

actual_topics: Section 1: Introduction, history, and scope of metastable states in heavy nuclei (pp. 1-3)

Section 2.2: Seniority isomers in spherical nuclei, Racah seniority algebra in single-j shell, B(E2) cancellation factor ((Omega-n)/(Omega-v))^2, and effective midshell (u^2-v^2)^2 (pp. 4-5)
Seniority v=2 (10+) and v=3 (27/2-) isomers in Sn isotopes (nu h11/2^n chain) from Zhang et al. [52] and Lozeva et al. [53] (pp. 5-6, Fig. 2)
Section 2.3: K-isomers in deformed nuclei, Nilsson model, pair breaking, and residual interactions (pp. 5-7, Fig. 3, Table 1)
Systematics of 6+ isomers in N=82 isotones (p. 7, Fig. 4)
which_figures_or_equations_checked: Figure 1: Nuclear chart showing distribution of isomers across Z and N (p. 3)
Figure 2: Compilation of B(E2) values for nu h11/2^2 and nu h11/2^3 chain in Sn isotopes (p. 5)
Figure 3: Schematic angular-momentum coupling: high-K vs spherical many-particle alignment (p. 5)
Figure 4: Half-life systematics of 6+ isomers in N=82 isotones (p. 7)
Table 1: Example two-quasiparticle excitations in prolate deformed nuclei (p. 6)
Formulas: T1/2^gamma = T1/2^level * (1+alpha)/b_total; B(E2) proportional to ((Omega-n)/(Omega-v))^2 and (u^2-v^2)^2 * e_eff^2; E_ex ~ sum sqrt((epsilon_k - epsilon_F)^2 + Delta^2) (pp. 4-6)
unverified_scope: Raw detector coincidence matrices and lifetime histograms of Zhang et al. [52] and Lozeva et al. [53]

audited_corrections: Sn isotope seniority U-shape is strictly for the nu h11/2^n subshell (10+ even, 27/2- odd), not all Sn isotopes or all states; the minimum occurs near the subshell midshell (A ~ 120-122), not 116Sn

documents.title: Isomer depletion
documents.canonical_source: J. J. Carroll and C. J. Chiara, Eur. Phys. J. Spec. Top. 233, 1151-1160 (2024)
documents.journal: The European Physical Journal Special Topics
documents.reading_depth: read (bounded review audit across 2 sequential chunks)

actual_topics: Section 1: Introduction, basic principles of isomer depletion, three-level topology (|0>, |m>, |d>), and energy release ratio (pp. 1151-1152, Fig. 1)
Section 2: Photon-induced depletion, Breit-Wigner integrated resonance cross section I_sigma, continuous bremsstrahlung vs monochromatic sources (pp. 1152-1153)
Photo-depletion of 180mTa: intermediate states at ~1.0 MeV and 2.8 MeV, level and decay schemes (pp. 1152-1154, Fig. 2, 3)
Photo-depletion of 108mAg via 1.28 MeV intermediate state (pp. 1154-1155, Fig. 4)

Critical review of the 178m2Hf controversy: Collins et al. 1999 claim of low-energy X-ray triggered decay refuted by independent investigations at SPring-8, Argonne, LANL, and LLNL; absence of low-energy coupling states (pp. 1154-1155)
which_figures_or_equations_checked: Figure 1: Schematic three-level diagram for isomer depletion and energy-gain illustration (p. 1152)
Figure 2: Level diagram for 180mTa depletion through intermediate states (p. 1153)
Figure 3: Decay scheme of 180Ta ground state and isomer (p. 1153)
Figure 4: Partial level scheme and potential depletion pathways for 108mAg (p. 1154)
Formula: Integrated resonance cross section I_sigma = int sigma(E) dE = ((pi*lambda_bar)^2 / 2) * g * (Gamma_m * Gamma_0 / Gamma_tot) (p. 1152)
unverified_scope: Raw bremsstrahlung spectral irradiance data from D-RAMS and S-DALINAC accelerators
Raw detector efficiency calibrations in 180mTa and 108mAg activation experiments
audited_corrections: Confirmed exact locators for the 178m2Hf controversy refutation (pp. 1154-1155)
Distinguished between verified photon-induced depletion in 180mTa/108mAg and refuted low-energy triggers in 178Hf

actual_topics: Section 3: Particle-induced isomer depletion: thermal and fast neutrons (177mLu, 180mTa, 242mAm), Coulomb excitation (pp. 1155-1156)
Section 4: Atomic-nuclear mechanisms: inverse electron bridge, NEET, and NEEC (pp. 1156-1158, Fig. 5, 6)

In-depth review of NEEC in 93mMo and associated controversies: Chiara et al. (Nature 2018) reported 1% depletion signal; Guo et al. (Nature 2021) challenged random coincidences; Chiara et al. (Nature 2021) replied with time gates; Guo et al. (PRL 2022) measured null limit P_exc < 2e-5; theoretical isolated-ion calculations yield 10^-10 to 10^-8 (pp. 1157-1158)

Authors' perspective and conflict of interest disclosure: C. J. Chiara was first author and J. J. Carroll was co-author of Chiara 2018; review argues that target-electron capture by moving ions in a solid medium differs fundamentally from vacuum isolated-ion calculations (bound electron momentum, excited configurations, vortex beams) (p. 1158)
Section 5: Depletion pathways and nuclear structure searches (186Re, 108Ag, 178Hf, 242Am) (pp. 1158-1159)
Section 6: Summary and outlook: XFEL, high-intensity lasers, storage rings, EBIT (p. 1159)
References 1 through 98 (p. 1160)
which_figures_or_equations_checked: Figure 5: Schematic diagrams comparing NEET and NEEC atomic-nuclear coupling (p. 1157)
Figure 6: Partial level scheme of 93Mo showing 21/2+ isomer and 4.85 keV intermediate state (p. 1157)
Critical citations: Chiara 2018 [83], Chiara 2021 [84], Guo 2021 [85], Wu 2019 [86], Guo 2022 [87], Bilous 2020 [90], Rzadkiewicz 2021 [91], Gargiulo 2022 [92], Wu 2022 [93] (p. 1158)
unverified_scope: Raw event-by-event data from ATLAS 2018 beamtime and HIRFL-CSR 2022 beamtime
Full independent recalculation of GOSIA Coulomb excitation and relativistic atomic wavefunctions
audited_corrections: Explicitly disclosed author co-authorship / interest in the Chiara 2018 Nature paper

Removed any simplistic claim of 'zero effect completely ended all experiments' or 'theory was definitively overthrown'; accurately portrayed the ongoing controversy between beam-catcher experimental setup and pure-beam null results, and the discrepancy with isolated-ion theory

summary_of_audited_overstatements.universal_fnu_100: Corrected across all sources: f_nu ~ 100 is Löbner's empirical rule of thumb, not a universal law; actual values span from f_nu ~ 2 (179W) to > 100 depending on nuclear structure and excitation energy.
summary_of_audited_overstatements.sn_isotopes_seniority_cancellation: Corrected: seniority cancellation in Sn is specific to the nu h11/2^n subshell (10+ in even, 27/2- in odd Sn), not all states or all Sn isotopes. WP20 Fig. 5 shows Pb, while Fig. 6 shows where Sn seniority breaks down.
summary_of_audited_overstatements.superheavy_fission_barrier_several_mev: Corrected: Dracoulis 2016 mentions static 1D barrier increase as a theoretical contention, but explicitly cautions that fission dynamics are missing and experimental fission widths are sparse.
summary_of_audited_overstatements.neec_controversy_status: Corrected: Carroll & Chiara 2024 is written by the discovery authors of Chiara 2018; they dispute the finality of Guo 2022's null result, citing different experimental conditions and condensed-matter target effects. The controversy remains an active, unresolved scientific debate.
